主要内容: On February 5, 2016, the Federal Reserve Bank (FRB) released a FEDS Note titled 'State and Local Pension Funding in the Enhanced Financial Accounts.' This report introduces new state-level data on the funding status of state and local government defined-benefit (DB) pension plans, which is part of the Enhanced Financial Accounts (EFA) initiative. Previously, the Financial Accounts of the United States reported aggregate levels of pension assets and liabilities in Table L.120.b. The new EFA tables and maps provide annual state-level detail on pension assets, liabilities, and various measures of funding status, going back to 2000. State and local governments have traditionally offered DB plans, while the private sector has largely moved to defined-contribution (DC) plans. In 2013, state and local DB pension entitlements totaled $4.9 trillion, compared to $0.5 trillion in DC arrangements. The funding status of these plans has received increased attention due to underfunded plans and debates over liability measurement methods. The note highlights that pension liabilities are calculated using different discount rates, with lower rates leading to higher present values and a worse funding outlook. The Government Accounting Standards Board (GASB) guidelines use expected returns on pension assets to calculate liabilities, resulting in higher discount rates and better funding appearances. Research suggests that lower discount rates should be used to reflect the lower risk of pension obligations due to legal protections. According to the Center for Retirement Research, state and local pension funds were underfunded by about $1 trillion in 2014. The report also discusses the estimation of plan assets using data from the Census survey and the BEA discount rate, which has varied over time. The findings are based on data from 1997 to 2014, with some gaps in state-by-state breakdowns for specific years.
